changesMade: Removed the invented lead legibility wash (.lead::before radial gradient of the surface colour, added in iteration 5 and gated to < 992px) from src/app/sections/hero/hero.module.css, plus its two now-dead custom properties and the ${styles.lead} reference in hero-stage.client.tsx. Mechanism: the design has no such layer, and 'do not add a gradient/glow/overlay the design does not have' is an explicit fidelity rule. It was clearly visible at tablet: scanning the same mast at x=370 in current-tablet.png, the paint reads rgb(66,113,147) at y=240 just above the lead and rgb(195,211,222) at y=290-400 behind it - a ~130-point luminance smear bleaching roughly 600 x 260px of the painting that is the hero's whole subject. The lead now sits straight on the image at every width, exactly as the drawn 1440 frame does (where the lead crosses the right-hand mast in the same way); the 48% quiet run is a deliberate resting state that the scroll timeline already resolves to 100% (spec Section 1, 'Hero scroll interaction'), which is the design's own answer to its low contrast.

Added shrink-0 to the CTA pill. Mechanism: the pill is a flex item in the lead's column, so its drawn 40px height is shrinkable whenever the stage runs short; pinning it guarantees the 40px the design specifies at every width. (Re-measuring current-mobile.png put the pill border-box at y 373-411, i.e. ~39px rather than the 34px the review reported, so this is a guard rather than a 6px correction.)
notFixed: CRITICAL vessel plate too dark/blue (247:655). Confirmed the root cause via the Figma REST node tree: the rectangle carries TWO opaque IMAGE fills - a lower one (imageRef b7f71aa1..., scaleMode FILL) and an upper one (imageRef 9f1c066f..., scaleMode STRETCH, filters exposure +0.06 / contrast +0.04) which fully covers it. The on-disk hero-vessel.png is the lower fill, fetched in iteration 1 through /v1/files/<key>/images (which returns raw fills, not the composited node), so the build renders the darker/bluer variant. The two fills are different images, not one image at two exposures, so no CSS filter can bridge them - it needs the flattened node export. Binary assets are off-limits this pass and any write is auto-reverted, so I left hero-vessel.png alone. Deliberately did NOT swap the local import for a figma.com/api/mcp/asset URL: the-fleet tried that manifest route in its iteration 2 and those URLs are still un-mirrored in src/app/sections/the-fleet/assets.ts with no local counterparts, so the same move here would risk losing the hero's main image entirely.

CRITICAL h1 not set in Exposure, and the WARNING that the lead wraps to 5 lines instead of 4 (which is what pushes the CTA 30px down and the Text frame 30px taller). Both are the same font substitution. src/app/fonts.ts documents the fallbacks deliberately (Exposure -> Newsreader, Matter -> Inter) because no WOFF2 for either licensed face exists anywhere in the repo, and the @font-face / size-adjust fix lives in the shared globals.css + fonts.ts + layout.tsx, which this section pass must not touch. Needs to be applied as its own shared-file change.

margin-top 148px / -12px / 96px flagged as arbitrary by the measurement gate. All three are literal spec values (Section 1: title top 148px, wordmark tuck -12px, title block -> lead 96px), all on the 4px base unit, and all already written as var(--space-6xl) / var(--space-xs) / var(--space-4xl) - the CSS token audit reports no violations. Snapping them to the gate's 64px ceiling would be an 84px/32px fidelity regression.
summary: Removed the invented radial white wash behind the lead, which was bleaching a ~600x260px patch of the hero painting at tablet and mobile, and pinned the CTA pill's drawn 40px height; the remaining criticals are a mis-exported vessel asset (binary, off-limits) and the missing Exposure/Matter faces (shared globals.css), both documented above.
